result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_gnp_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add an Erdős-Rényi G(n,p) random graph to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3734-L3797){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_gnp_graph( n, p, directed=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![G(n, p) random graph](/assets/graphs/add-gnp-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three random graphs on the same ring of eight nodes for edge probability p=0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. Each possible edge appears independently, so the drawings gain edges as p grows (3, 8, and 14 here) with no pattern to which pairs are joined." width="100%"} Each possible edge is included independently with probability `p`. This model is useful for generating random graphs with a specific edge density. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes to add. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of edge creation, in range of `[0.0, 1.0]`. [directed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[bool]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If provided and differs from graph's directed setting, creates a temporary graph with the specified directedness. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each of the `n(n-1)/2` possible edges is included independently with probability `p`, so the expected edge count is `n(n-1)/2 * p` -- for `n=50` and `p=0.1` that's about `245` edges on average, though the exact count varies with the random seed: ::: {#94435ba8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_gnp_graph(n=50, p=0.1, seed=23) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (50, 109) ``` ::: :::
